statements.text: The task model carries a nullable deletion timestamp serialized in JSON as `deletedAt`: an ISO-8601 string once the task is soft-deleted, and `null` while the task is active.
`DELETE /tasks/{id}` on an existing task soft-deletes it — it sets `deletedAt` to the current time and returns HTTP 204 No Content.
`DELETE /tasks/{id}` does not permanently remove the task: after deletion the task is still present in the store and still returned by `GET /tasks?includeDeleted=true`.
`DELETE /tasks/{id}` for an id that is not in the store returns HTTP 404 Not Found.
`GET /tasks` returns only active tasks by default: a soft-deleted task does not appear in the response.
`GET /tasks?includeDeleted=true` returns all tasks, including soft-deleted ones, whose `deletedAt` is non-null.
`GET /tasks/{id}` returns HTTP 404 Not Found for a soft-deleted task.
The four seeded tasks remain active after startup: each is returned by `GET /tasks` with `deletedAt` of `null`.

The other CRUD endpoints (`POST /tasks`, `PUT /tasks/{id}`, `GET /tasks/{id}` for active tasks, blank-title rejection) keep their existing behaviour; the 5 baseline tests still pass and `dotnet build` stays clean.
`Domain/**` gains no dependency on the HTTP layer (R-004) and the `TaskState` naming is unchanged (R-005); the change stays inside `src/TaskTracker.Api` and `tests/TaskTracker.Tests`.

`DELETE /tasks/{id}` for a task that is already soft-deleted returns HTTP 404 Not Found and leaves the original `deletedAt` untouched — a soft-deleted task is treated as absent by every id-addressed endpoint.
`PUT /tasks/{id}` for a soft-deleted task returns HTTP 404 Not Found, consistently with `GET /tasks/{id}` and `DELETE /tasks/{id}`.
